findings.expected: MR03 and the helper fix one outcome when two eligible misread data have the same first earned A/B, independent of input order; the helper enforces question order and first_use_part.
findings.actual: MR03 does not say what happens when a datum's first earned A/B has already absorbed another datum's deduction, and the helper silently moves on or charges nothing. The helper's result depends on the order of the datums list: awards X(a,B,[d1,d2]) and Y(b,A,[d1]) give net 1/2 for [d1,d2] (d2 charged nothing) and 0/2 for [d2,d1]. With one shared A/B only (T2), the second datum costs nothing, and the ledger says 'no available earned A/B on this datum anywhere', contradicting MR03's 'Deduct nothing only if no A/B is earned on the datum anywhere'. The helper also accepts a datum whose first_use_part differs from its first tagged award (T10) and takes list order as question order without checking (T11). The meaning of 'on that datum' is set by author tags: stationary WO:118/:120 tag and deduct the derivative slots P2/I1, which do not depend on the misread constant. A value-dependence reading would instead give 5/6, not 4/6, when the I3 y-value is also slipped.
findings.evidence: SCRATCH/shared/ledger_tests.py (copy of helper, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE): T2 net 1 with ledger ('q', None, 0); T3a net 1 vs T3b net 0; T10/T11 accepted. No current fixture is affected: the only multi-datum fixture (trig RF-two-distinct-copied-data) has disjoint first A/Bs (a-B1 tagged [a] only), so it is order-invariant.
findings.repair: For E/F (or a one-line MR03-OPS addition): settle data in first-use order, let each datum take its first earned A/B not already charged, and state the outcome when none remains. Define 'on that datum' as the tag convention, i.e. any A/B in work that starts from the misread data. In the helper, sort by declared part order, assert first_use_part matches the first tagged award, and add order-permutation fixtures.
